chunks: What al-Shaykh—may Allah the Exalted support him—informed me of, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, from his brother al-Husayn, from 'Ali ibn Yaqtin, who said:
I asked Aba al-Hasan عليه السلام about ghusl (ritual bath) on Friday, al-Adha, and al-Fitr. He said: "It is a sunnah (prophetic tradition), and it is not obligatory."

key_terms.الْأَضْحَى: Eid al-Adha, the festival of sacrifice
key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: ghusl (ritual bath) performed for ritual purification
key_terms.الْفِطْرِ: Eid al-Fitr, the festival marking the end of fasting
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: a recommended prophetic tradition, not mandatory

ai.seo_question: Is ghusl for Friday and the two Eids obligatory or recommended in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that ghusl (ritual bath) for Friday, Eid al-Adha, and Eid al-Fitr is sunnah (prophetic tradition) rather than an obligation. It is a jurisprudential report clarifying the recommended status of these ritual baths in acts of worship.
